transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

I’ve been having hallucinations that are really starting to scare me and make it hard to get through the day. I’m not sure what’s real sometimes, and it’s getting worse, so I wanted to get some help with that.
Have you been using marijuana or cannabis recently or in the past few months, and if so, did your hallucinations start or get worse around the times you were using it?
I don’t use marijuana or cannabis and haven’t for at least the past few months. I didn’t notice any connection between that and when the hallucinations started or got worse.
How long have you been experiencing these hallucinations—days to weeks, or has it been going on for several months or longer?
It’s been going on for quite a while now, almost two years. I’d say about 1 year and 11 months since I first started noticing the hallucinations.

During the times you have these hallucinations, are you also having periods of feeling extremely depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks at a time, or do the hallucinations sometimes occur even when your mood feels relatively normal?

The hallucinations happen even when my mood feels more or less normal. I do get down or stressed sometimes because of them, but I haven’t noticed long stretches of feeling extremely depressed for weeks at a time tied to when they happen.

Besides the hallucinations, have you had strong beliefs that others say are not true—like feeling people are watching, plotting against you, or that you have special powers or a special mission—that you’re completely convinced about?

I’m not really sure about that. Sometimes I get suspicious that people might be watching me or talking about me, but I wouldn’t say I’m completely convinced it’s true, and I usually end up doubting myself.

Over these nearly two years, have you noticed a clear decline in your ability to function—like worsening performance at work or school, withdrawing from friends or family, or struggling more with everyday tasks—compared to how you were before the hallucinations started?

Yeah, things have definitely gotten worse over that time. I’ve had more trouble keeping up with work and basic stuff like cleaning or cooking, and I don’t really feel like seeing friends or doing things I used to enjoy anymore. It’s been a gradual slide, but looking back I can see I’m not functioning like I used to before the hallucinations started.

Have you noticed your thoughts or speech becoming disorganized—like losing your train of thought, jumping between unrelated ideas, or people saying they find it hard to follow what you’re saying—over this time?

Yeah, that’s been happening more over this time. I’ll start talking and then lose my train of thought or jump to something unrelated, and people sometimes tell me they can’t really follow what I’m trying to say.
Over this period, have you noticed feeling emotionally flat or blank, speaking much less than you used to, or having very little motivation or energy to start even simple activities most days?

Yeah, I’ve noticed all of that over this time. People tell me I seem kind of flat or blank, I don’t talk as much as I used to, and it’s really hard to get myself to start simple things like showering, cooking, or leaving the house most days.

There is no temporal link to substance use, and no sustained, severe mood episodes that would suggest a primary mood disorder with psychotic features. These features fit the more specific subtype characterized by prominent negative symptoms and typical course, so the nonspecific code (F20.9) is no longer needed and is replaced with the more specific F20.0. Given the strength and completeness of the syndrome description, I consider this sufficient for a confident working diagnosis, so I am marking this as final.
